questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT:

options.text: Have scratches on it.
Give you a clear view on both sides.
Be airtight.
Fasten securely to your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, let you see clearly to both sides, fasten securely, and allow air to flow through. An airtight shield will fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to do only one action.
Skip swerving and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. This can cause your motorcycle to tip over. Instead, brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed even if you wear a helmet.
Only needed on windy days.
Not needed if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed even if you wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can hurt your hearing, even with a helmet on. Hearing protection lets you stay safe while still hearing important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop ahead
Turn on high beams
Turn right
Hazard in the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard in the road
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in a group talk to each other. When the lead rider puts their right leg out to the side, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for a long time can cause all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Tiredness.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, tiredness, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to stay warm and safe.

questions.question: When riding in traffic and a small animal enters your lane, you should:

options.text: Swerve into another lane to avoid hitting it.
Switch lanes as fast as you can.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane to avoid hitting another vehicle. Swerving into traffic to miss a small animal can cause a crash. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: The right footwear for motorcycle riding should have:

options.text: Long, loose laces.
Short heels.
Tall heels.
Always be sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Choose short heels because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in any laces so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and bikes with sidecars turn differently than regular motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look ahead.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look ahead.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: How do you keep other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Move side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This discourages car drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show road rules like speed limits. These signs are white with black text or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you want to go.
Do not drag your feet on the road.
Avoid looking at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow to a safe speed before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet on the road or you may lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: Flash your brake light when:

options.text: You are approaching a police officer.
Someone is following too closely.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is following you too closely. The other driver may not see a danger ahead and may not know you are slowing down. Also flash your brake light before you slow in places where drivers might not expect you to stop.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they seem to be:

options.text: Going faster than they actually are.
Going slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are moving.
Closer than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles often appear to be traveling faster than they really are.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or always bad. Choose your lane position based on the riding conditions.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while turning, you should:

options.text: Straighten the motorcycle, square the handlebars, then stop.
Use both brakes hard while leaning.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the motorcycle, square the handlebars, then stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop while turning, first straighten the motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply the brakes slowly, reduce your lean angle, then apply more brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: To turn a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlebar grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Not touch the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When going faster than a walk, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Push the grip in the direction you want to turn to lean the right way.

questions.question: When stopped, you should:

options.text: Stay in first gear.
Stay in neutral.
Stay in fifth gear.
Stay in any gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in first gear.
questions.explanation: Downshift through the gears as you slow and stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Of crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by drivers not yielding the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
More than 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: More than 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel starts to skid?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, how much distance should you keep between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead during normal conditions. Increase this distance when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
Only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can permanently damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs and other hearing protection block damage while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily buildup. What should you do about it?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride on it because it gives better grip.
Stay away from the entire center portion of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips in the center of each lane. When the road is dry, it usually has enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it while staying in the center of your lane. Avoid it when roads are wet.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle tries to pass you from behind?

options.text: Move to the center portion of the lane.
Move to the left portion of the lane.
Move to the right portion of the lane.
Your lane position does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: Always the right portion of the lane.
Always the center portion of the lane.
Always the left portion of the lane.
It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on current road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: Both brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Only use the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides at least 70 percent of your stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.
Move onto the shoulder.
Turn on your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, stay in the center of your lane. Getting closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: Which of these will protect your eyes from wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from having to chase the group. It also allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help them.
